facts: $\underset{\sim}{i}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix}$ runs one unit along the positive $x$-axis and $\underset{\sim}{j}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}$ one unit along the positive $y$-axis.
Every vector splits in exactly one way as $\underset{\sim}{a}=x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}$, where $x\underset{\sim}{i}$ is its horizontal component vector.
Given a magnitude $r$ and an angle of inclination $\theta$, the components are $x=r\cos\theta$ and $y=r\sin\theta$.
The cosine belongs to the axis the angle is measured from, so always check which axis $\theta$ starts at.
For a true bearing $\beta$, measured from north, the east component is $r\sin\beta$ and the north component is $r\cos\beta$.
The signs of the components come out of $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ automatically, so no extra sign rule is needed.
steps: Decide whether the vector is given by components or by a magnitude and an angle.
For a magnitude and an angle of inclination, use $x=r\cos\theta$ and $y=r\sin\theta$.
For a true bearing $\beta$, use east $=r\sin\beta$ and north $=r\cos\beta$.
Write the answer as $x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}$, rounding only at the end.

foundation.question_text: Write $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-9\end{pmatrix}$ as the sum of its horizontal and vertical component vectors.
State the horizontal and vertical component vectors of $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\8\end{pmatrix}$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{b}=0\underset{\sim}{i}+8\underset{\sim}{j}$
The horizontal component vector is $0\underset{\sim}{i}$ and the vertical component vector is $8\underset{\sim}{j}$.

foundation.question_text: A vector has magnitude $10$ and an angle of inclination of $30^{\circ}$. Write it in exact component form.
A vector has magnitude $8$ and an angle of inclination of $60^{\circ}$. Write it in exact component form.
A vector has magnitude $12$ and an angle of inclination of $135^{\circ}$. Write it in exact component form.
A vector has magnitude $6$ and an angle of inclination of $210^{\circ}$. Write it in exact component form.

foundation.solution_text:
The arrow runs $3$ units left and $5$ units up.
$\underset{\sim}{a}=-3\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$

The arrow runs $6$ units right and $5$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{b}=6\underset{\sim}{i}-5\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.question_text: A plane flies on a true bearing of $048^{\circ}$ and its velocity has an eastward component of $180$ km/h. Find the plane's speed, to the nearest kilometre per hour.
A vector has magnitude $26$ and an acute angle of inclination $\theta$ with $\tan\theta=\frac{5}{12}$. Write the vector in exact component form.
mastery.solution_text:
Since $\tan\theta=\frac{5}{12}$ and $\theta$ is acute, the right-angled triangle has sides $5$, $12$ and $13$.
$\cos\theta=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}$
$x=26\times\frac{12}{13}$
$=24$
$y=26\times\frac{5}{13}$
$=10$
The vector is $24\underset{\sim}{i}+10\underset{\sim}{j}$.

mastery.question_text: A yacht sails $30$ km on a true bearing of $125^{\circ}$. How far east and how far south of its start is it, each correct to one decimal place?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{east}=30\sin 125^{\circ}$
$=24.5746\ldots$
$\approx 24.6$
$\text{north}=30\cos 125^{\circ}$
$=-17.2073\ldots$
$\approx -17.2$
The yacht is $24.6$ km east and $17.2$ km south of its start.
